nodes.name: \bf Proposition 4.2.2: tabular c $\textup{Gr}^{r}_{\textup{F}}\circ\phi_*[r]$ $t$ -exact tabular
nodes.statement: Let $\phi \colon Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be a quasi-finite morphism. Then $\textup{Gr}^{r}_{\textup{F}}\circ \phi_{*}[r]$ is left $t$-exact. Moreover, if $Z$ is affine over $S$, then it is $t$-exact.

nodes.name: \bf Proposition 5.2.1: tabular c ${\mathcal R}_{d} \circ \phi_{*}$ right $t$ -exact…
nodes.statement:
Let $\phi \colon Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be a quasi-finite morphism. Then 
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item  ${\mathcal R}_{d!}[d-N+1] \circ \phi_{*}$ is left $t$-exact.
        \item  Moreover if $Z/S$ is affine, ${\mathcal R}_{d!} \circ \phi_{*}$ and ${\mathcal R}_{d} \circ \phi_{*}$ are right $t$-exact.
    \end{enumerate}

nodes.statement: Let $\phi \colon Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be a quasi-finite morphism. Then ${\mathcal R}_{N-1!} \circ \phi_*$ is left $t$-exact and  ${\mathcal R}_{N-1*} \circ \phi_!$ is right $t$-exact. Moreover, if $Z/S$ is affine then they are both $t$-exact.

nodes.name: \bf Theorem 2.2.2: tabular c Beilinson's basic tabular
nodes.statement:
(Beilinson)
Let $\phi: Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be a quasi-finite\footnote{In [deCM10] this is stated for $\phi$ an affine open immersion.} and affine morphism. Let $\mathrm{K}$ perverse. Then 
 \begin{enumerate}[(b)]
     \item the cohomology groups ${\rm H}^{i}(Z,j_{1!}j_{1}^{!}j_{2*}j_{2}^*\mathrm{K})$ vanish for $i \neq 0$, here $j_{r} \colon V_r \hookrightarrow Z,r=1,2$ are inverse images (under $\phi$) of generic hyperplane section complements.
     \item If $Z$ is itself affine then, ${\rm H}^i(Z,j_{!}j^!\mathrm{K})=0$ for $i \neq 0$. Here $j \colon V \hookrightarrow Z$ is the inverse image (under $\phi$) of a generic hyperplane section complement.
 \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: \bf Corollary 5.4.2: tabular c Deligne's weak Lefschetz for upper semi-perverse sheaves tabular
nodes.statement: Let $\phi: Z \to {\mathbb P}$ be a quasi-finite. Let $\mathrm{K}$ be an upper semi-perverse sheaf on $Z$. Then the cohomology groups $\mathrm{H}^i(Z,j_{!}j^!\mathrm{K})=0$ vanish for $i < 0$. Here $j \colon V \hookrightarrow Z$ is the inverse image (under $\phi$) of a generic hyperplane section complement.

nodes.name: \bf Proposition 6.1.2: tabular c Weak Lefschetz for Gysin tabular
nodes.statement:
Then for a general hyperplane section $\Lambda \subset {\mathbb A}^N$, the Gysin map 
    \[
    {\rm H}^{r-2}_c \left (\Lambda \backslash (\Lambda \cap Z), {\mathbb Q}_{\ell} \right )(-1) \to {\rm H}_c^{r}({\mathbb A}^N \backslash Z, {\mathbb Q}_{\ell}),
    \]
    \noindent is a surjection for $r-1>\textup{dim}(Z)$.

nodes.name: \bf Theorem 2.3.1: tabular c Sharpening of Esnault-Katz bound tabular
nodes.statement:
The eigenvalues of the geometric Frobenius acting on 
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
    \item ${\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j}(Z)$, for $j\geq 0$ and,
    \item ${\rm H}_c^{\textup{dim}(Z)+j+1}({\mathbb A}^N\backslash Z)$ for $0 \leq j \leq \textup{dim}(Z)+1$
\end{enumerate}
    \noindent are divisible by $q^{\mu_j(N;d_1,d_2 \cdots,d_r)}$ (see Equation (6.2)).

nodes.name: \bf Theorem A.3.1, \bf Proposition A.5.1: tabular c Beilinson $t$ -structure on…
nodes.statement:
(Beilinson)
    The subcategories $({}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\leq 0},{}^p{\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}^{\geq 0})$ define a $t$-structure on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$.

${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ is a symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category and the Beilinson $t$-structure (from ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{indcons}}(X)$) restricts to one on ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$. Moreover
    \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
        \item an object $\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ in  ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$ is in the heart of the Beilinson $t$-structure iff $\textup{Gr}^{i}[i]\mathrm{K}^{\bullet}$ are perverse.
        \item The functor $\textup{Dec}$ (see Definition A.4.4) preserves the subcategory ${\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(X)$. 
    \end{enumerate}

nodes.name: \bf Proposition 7.2.1: tabular c $\textup{F}$ is $t$ -exact tabular
nodes.statement: The functor $\textup{F} \circ \phi_* \colon {\mathcal D}_{\textup{cons}}(Z) \to {\mathcal D} F_{\textup{cons}}(\textup{Fl})$ is left $t$-exact. Moreover, if $Z/S$ is affine then it is $t$-exact.

nodes.name: \bf Theorem 7.2.2: tabular c P= Dec F as functors tabular
nodes.statement:
There is a natural equivalence of functors
  \[
  \mathrm{P} \circ \phi_* \simeq \mathrm{Dec}(\mathrm{F}\circ\phi_*).
  \]

nodes.name: \bf Corollary 7.2.3: tabular c Equality of spectral sequences in ${\mathcal P}(\textup{Fl})$ tabular
nodes.statement:
For any sheaf $\mathrm{K}$ on $Z$, there is a natural (in $\mathrm{K}$) isomorphism\footnote{The isomorphism of the spectral sequences could also have been obtained using Postnikov systems at the level of derived categories, a detour to the $(\infty,1)$-world is not necessary.} between the constant perverse spectral sequence
   \[
   E_1^{i,j}={^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}{^p\mathcal{H}}^{-j}(\phi_*\mathrm{K})[j]) \implies {^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\phi_*\mathrm{K})
   \]
   \noindent and the  d\'ecal\'ee of the universal flag filtration spectral sequence
   \[
   E_1^{i,j}={^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\textup{Gr}^{-j}_{\textup{F}}\phi_*\mathrm{K}[j]) \implies {^p\mathcal{H}}^{i+j}(\overline{\pi}^{\vee}_{*}\overline{\pi}^{\dagger}\phi_*\mathrm{K}).
   \]
